content: The purpose of these interviews is to help men and women better understand their experiences and needs related to HIV and other health issues. This information sheet provides a detailed written explanation of the interview process. Before the phone interview begins, the interviewer will verbally explain this information to you again. You are encouraged to ask any questions about the interview process if there is anything you do not fully understand. Once you understand all aspects of the interview, you will be asked to decide whether or not you wish to participate. If you agree to participate verbally over the phone, you will be provided with a written copy of this information sheet for your records. It is important to note that your participation in this interview is entirely voluntary, and you are not obligated to take part if you do not wish to. The World Health Organization (WHO) HIV Department is conducting these interviews to gain a deeper understanding of the HIV-related needs of transgender women and men on a global scale. Specifically, the study aims to explore HIV-related risk behaviors, experiences with HIV and other healthcare services, and the challenges and opportunities for effective HIV prevention, treatment, and care among transgender individuals. The findings from this study will inform WHO’s recommendations for HIV guidelines tailored to key populations, including transgender people. You are being invited to participate because you are a transgender individual who has expressed interest in being interviewed by completing the recent online survey titled “Transgender People Short Survey.” Approximately 20 transgender individuals will participate in this study. If you agree to take part in the interview, you will be asked to provide a telephone number or Skype account name where you can be reached, as well as a date and time that is convenient for you. The interviewer will contact you at the agreed-upon time and conduct a phone interview lasting approximately one hour. The interview will follow a semi-structured format, meaning the interviewer will ask guiding questions but will also allow you to respond freely and discuss any topics that are important to you. The interviews will be voice-recorded and later transcribed by the interviewer. The transcribed content will be analyzed, and a report of the findings will be written and published. The report may include direct quotes from your interview and others, but no identifying information will be included. There are some potential risks or discomforts associated with participating in this study. The interview will include personal questions about your past and current sexual activity, drug use, and transitioning experiences, which may make you feel shy or uncomfortable. You are not required to answer any questions you do not wish to, and you can simply decline to answer during the interview. There are no direct benefits to you for participating in this study. However, WHO will gain valuable insights into how transgender women and men are affected by HIV and other health issues, which will help improve understanding of their needs for HIV prevention, treatment, and care. All information about you will be handled as confidentially as possible. While participation in research may involve some loss of privacy, your data will be protected. A study file with your interview ID number will be created electronically, and the recording and transcript of your interview will be stored in this file. Only the interviewer and the research team will have access to this file. After the analysis of the interviews is completed, all personal identifying information and recordings will be deleted. The transcribed interviews will be stored electronically and published as part of a report. Any published information, whether in writing or presented at scientific meetings, will not include your name or other personal identifying details. You will not receive any compensation for participating in this interview. If you decide to participate, the interview will last approximately 60 minutes (1 hour). Participation in these interviews is entirely voluntary. You may choose to participate or not, and you can leave the interview at any time without providing an explanation. There will be no penalties or loss of rights regardless of your decision. If you have any questions about the interview process, you are encouraged to ask. Participation in these interviews is voluntary, and you can decline to participate at any point without any penalty or loss of rights.
